# 1 Clement Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 17

**17:1** Let us also be imitators of those who went about in goatskins and sheepskins, heralding the coming of Christ. We speak of Elijah and Elisha, and also of Ezekiel, the prophets; and in addition of those who have received testimony.

**17:2** Abraham received testimony and was called "Friend of God," and he says, gazing on the glory of God with humble mind, "I am but dust and ashes." [Gen 18:27]

**17:3** And again, concerning Job it is written thus: "Job was righteous and blameless, true and godly, one who kept himself from all evil." [Job 1:1, 8 LXX]

**17:4** But he himself, accusing himself, says: "No man is clean from filth, not even if his life is a single day." [Job 14:4-5 LXX]

**17:5** Moses was called "faithful in all his house," and through his ministry God judged Egypt with scourges and torments; but even he, glorified, said not a word of loftiness for himself, but when the oracle was given to him from the burning bush, he said, "Who am I, that you should send me? I am weak in speech and slow of tongue." [Num 12:7; Exod 3:10-11; 4:10 LXX]

**17:6** And again he says: "I am vapor from the cauldron." [Num 11:14-15 - paraphrase, or LXX variant]

---

*EMET: The "goatskins and sheepskins" alludes to Heb 11:37-38. Clement is drawing on a tradition of prophetic humility from Abraham to Job to Moses. "Dust and ashes" is among the most poignant of the humility-formulas.*
